recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow non-substantive narrative fix on an active current-build page, preserves the later datatype terminology decision, and does not change conformance semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-18357 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core technical correction requesting clearer wording for the extensibility page sentence that said constructing a primitive value just to satisfy data rules would be a bad idea and a disallowed modifier extension.
initial_application: The request was partially applied by commit 7bf7397f4a965784698e0d343f8a96789cdf4942, which changed the old sentence to mention simple data types but left the awkward phrase 'both a bad idea as well as a modifier extension' and a less direct 'which is not allowed' clause.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini maps extension=extensibility, confirming source/extensibility.html is active build input. Later issue FHIR-25431 and commit 8592e1207273b786db340efb927bb6d1dc9756c9 standardized this sentence from 'simple data types' to 'simple datatypes', so the reconciliation preserved that later spelling. Jira phrase search found only FHIR-18357, and direct Zulip/Confluence FHIR-18357 searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Changed source/extensibility.html to remove the redundant 'both' and state directly that modifier extensions are not allowed on simple datatypes.
source_changes: source/extensibility.html: clarified the sentence to say 'This would be a bad idea as well as a modifier extension, and modifier extensions are not allowed on simple datatypes.'

related_jiras.note: Standardized 'data type' to 'datatype' after FHIR-18357 and explains why this fix preserved 'simple datatypes' rather than reverting to the older proposed spelling.
